events.headline: Democrats swept the Nov. 3 US midterms, flipping both the House (~250 seats) and Senate (~54 seats); VP Vance blamed the Iran war for the GOP loss, which markets read as raising Washington's incentive for an Iran diplomatic deal. AI/data-center and large-cap tech names fell on fears of a data-center cost/regulation crackdown under a Democratic Congress, while healthcare names were flagged as likely beneficiaries

WTI crude tumbled more than 8% on Nov. 4 to ~$88/bbl (Brent ~$97) on hopes for a US-Iran deal and a possible Strait of Hormuz reopening -- the single biggest driver of Wall Street's ~3% Dow rally. Unconfirmed IRGC reports of tanker/tugboat fires and a mine strike in the Strait add two-sided uncertainty to the de-escalation narrative

Asian and US chip/AI-infrastructure stocks sold off sharply on renewed AI-capex/bubble concerns: SK Hynix -~9%, Samsung -~6.7%, Advantest -~11.7%, Lasertec -~11.8%, Tokyo Electron -~10% (Kospi -~4.8%, triggering a program-trading halt); Nvidia, AMD, CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN fell on Wall Street on slower data-center spending fears; Qualcomm (-~7.4% after-hours) and Arm (-~2% after-hours) fell on higher capex / softer guidance despite beating estimates

China's one-year suspension of its expanded October 2025 export controls on rare earths, rare-earth processing equipment and lithium-battery/graphite materials is set to expire Nov. 10, 2026, with no official word yet from the Ministry of Commerce on an extension, narrowing, or lapse -- a near-term supply overhang for materials names

Walmart (+~3%) and other defensive/consumer names led the Dow's ~3% rally (best day since April 2025) as sharply cheaper oil and falling Treasury yields boosted the consumer/goods outlook; gold jumped ~3% to near $4,135/oz on the same lower-oil, weaker-dollar, lower-yield mix
